theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Energy (+2.48%) and Utilities (+1.15%) led the market today, while Technology (-2.51%) and Consumer Discretionary (-0.84%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.00% versus +0.56% for defensives and +0.69% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.34% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -2.14%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.66%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 21.45% to 19.99, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.42% to $4,186.70, crude oil was little changed at $99.04, and bitcoin slipped 0.60% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
